title: Naturality comparison for the tensor–Hom and Verdier exchanges
statement:
Fix a six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use its constructible finite-Tor categories and completed, rationalized, or common-stage operations, respectively. Let $X$ be smooth, separated of finite type and geometrically connected of pure dimension $d$ over $k$, let $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $a:X	o s$ be its structure morphism, and let $K\in\Dctf(X,\Lambda)$ satisfy the hypotheses of [sk-thm-sf-global-duality] and [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom]. Put $C=Ra_!K$ and $\omega_s=R\mathrm{id}_s^!\Lambda_s$. Let $
u:\omega_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ be the identity counit and put $c=Ra^!(
u)$, whose isomorphism and counit compatibility are supplied at each of the four stages by [lem-sf-identification-coefficient-transport]. Let $b_{\omega}$ and $b_1$ denote the tensor–internal-Hom exchange isomorphisms [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom] at $N=\omega_s$ and $N=\Lambda_s$, respectively. If $\eta_K:\mathbb D_sC	o Ra_*\mathbb D_XK$ is the Verdier exchange map constructed with $b_{\omega}$ and $R\mathcal Hom_X(K,c)$, then naturality in $N$ gives
$$b_1\circ Ra_*R\mathcal Hom_X(K,c)=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,
u)\circ b_{\omega},$$
so $\eta_K=b_1^{-1}\circ R\mathcal Hom_s(C,
u)$. If $\alpha_C$ is the point comparison obtained using $
u$ and $\alpha_C^1$ is the comparison obtained using $\Lambda_s$, then
$$\alpha_C=\alpha_C^1\circ\operatorname{Fib}_sR\mathcal Hom_s(C,
u),$$
where $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ is the point fibre. Consequently the global-duality map built from $\eta_K$ is
$$G=\operatorname{Fib}_s(b_1^{-1})\circ(\alpha_C^1)^{-1}.$$ The displayed equations hold in the actual category at the chosen coefficient stage, with $b_{\omega}$ and $b_1$ the exchanges at that stage; their naturality in $N$ is the naturality asserted in [sk-thm-sf-tensor-hom].
